heroLead: Altamont sits at the very core of the field that shares its name, and mineral interests here trade differently than almost anywhere else in the basin.
intro: Altamont gave its name to the Altamont-Bluebell field, and that is not a coincidence — this stretch of Duchesne County has been drilled continuously since the 1950s for its signature paraffin-rich, waxy crude. Wells here have run deep for the basin, some past 15,000 feet, chasing Green River and Wasatch bench targets that hold up well over long production lives. If you own minerals under or near Altamont, you likely hold an interest in one of the most consistently studied trends in the Uinta Basin.

We buy fractional and full mineral interests around Altamont directly from owners, confirming your specific well or unit against Utah Division of Oil, Gas and Mining records before we put a number in writing.

sections.heading: Deep bench drilling and long-lived production
paragraphs: The wells that made Altamont's name typically target multiple stacked Green River and lower Wasatch benches, and because completions here have historically been vertical or directional rather than the newer horizontal style seen elsewhere, decline curves tend to be gentler and more predictable once a well passes its first few years. That steadiness is part of why family-held interests around Altamont often show up as small but reliable monthly royalty checks going back decades rather than a recent lump of activity.

sections.heading: Ownership around Altamont
paragraphs: Much of the acreage in and around Altamont was homesteaded and later leased for oil and gas as the field developed, and it is common for the mineral estate to have been divided among heirs multiple times since. We frequently work with sellers who hold a modest fraction of a section — sometimes a few percent — and want a clear answer on what that specific fraction is worth rather than a rough countywide estimate.

faqs.question: Is Altamont acreage generally worth more than acreage elsewhere in Duchesne County?
faqs.answer: It can be, since it sits in the historic core of the field with deep, long-lived wells, but we still price against your specific well data rather than a location premium alone.

faqs.question: My check has been the same small amount for years. Is that normal for Altamont?
faqs.answer: Yes, this field is known for gentle, long-tail decline once a well matures, so a steady modest check is typical rather than a warning sign.

faqs.question: I only own a small fractional interest. Is it worth selling?
faqs.answer: Often yes. We routinely buy fractional interests as small as a few percent of a unit and will give you a straight answer based on your actual share.
